cards.anchor: The valued outcome is three elevation-vial attenuations with normalized spread at most 4 percent at second 120, reducing stirring time if feasible. One stipulated 300 rpm trial stopped at second 60 and produced 0.204, 0.209 and 0.207, approximately 2.4 percent spread. This bounds a counterexample to universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm; it does not establish repeatability or harm from longer agitation.
cards.burden: Six fresh trials exhaust the 90-minute session allowance. Manual five-second image logging, references, rinsing and three withdrawals within ten seconds require preparation. Record all sample failures and actual stirring and quiet durations. Use the spill tray and immediately stop if liquid escapes. No unavailable measurement equipment is indispensable.
cards.construction: Hypothesis-testing construction: run three fresh-recipe pairs at commanded 900 rpm from second zero, comparing fixed 60-second and 105-second doses. Preassign duration order as short/long, long/short, short/long. Use 150 mL tap water and 0.30 mL dye in the 250 mL beaker, one bottle, fixed addition location and locked camera settings; rinse between trials. Optical checks never extend or restart stirring. Sample at second 120, withdrawing 1 mL at 10, 28 and 45 mm within ten seconds; alternate ascending and descending sampling order within each pair. Use water-only and common-aliquot references per block. Log five-second side spread, depression, speck frames, commanded speed, cessation times and final raw vial readings. Compute final spread as max-minus-min divided by mean.
cards.defeat: The proposed adverse opening is defeated for this bounded comparison if the recurrent paired pattern of long-dose failure with short-dose success does not appear, especially if 105 seconds repeatedly rescues 60-second failures. Both targets passing despite worse long-dose images supports interface cost without demonstrated sample harm. Both failing or inconsistent pairs leave the comparison inconclusive. Even the adverse pattern cannot isolate agitation damage from the unequal quiet intervals.
cards.mutation: Replace image-controlled continuation with preassigned exposure doses. Test the hypothesis that an operation intended to obtain uniformity can worsen the independent sample proxy when extended. This severs optical control but cannot demonstrate the proposed disturbance-to-continuation return loop.
cards.prediction_candidate: Hypothesis A predicts recurrent pairs in which the 105-second trial has final-vial spread above 4 percent and the 60-second trial has spread at most 4 percent. Such a result would support adversity of the longer-exposure, shorter-recovery regime under these conditions. Greater side spread or specks alone would support only an optical-interface cost.
cards.prediction_rival: Rival B predicts that 105 seconds preserves or improves final-vial spread relative to 60 seconds, potentially bringing short-dose failures below the 4 percent target. Both passing is compatible with this rival even if long-dose images fluctuate. Neither outcome establishes necessity of 900 rpm or of the preferred optical rule.
cards.probe: Compare final-vial target status and raw normalized spreads within each preassigned pair, retaining all three pairs. The separating observation is recurring long-dose failure paired with short-dose success versus long-dose preservation or rescue. Treat side images, specks and depression as secondary signals; record actual quiet durations of 60 versus 15 seconds because the measured intervention combines dose and recovery time.
cards.rival: Hypothesis B: extra agitation preserves or improves the bounded sample proxy, and fluctuating images can reflect disturbances without adverse depth-vial consequences. The bright specks have no established identity. A useful longer dose would not establish that optical feedback or 900 rpm is necessary.
unknowns: No matched 900 rpm final-vial observations are supplied; every dose effect and repeat success remains hypothetical.
Different cessation times yield different quiet intervals before second 120; this probe cannot separate additional stirring from recovery, settling or transport.
Specks may be bubbles, reflections or undissolved dye; their causal contribution and bubble fraction remain unmeasured.
Sampling can disturb gradients, common-aliquot repeatability is not concentration calibration, and commanded rpm has no independent verification.
Three pairs provide limited replication; reversal and sampling-order alternation reduce but do not remove order effects.
The fixed-dose comparison does not establish actual optical-rule prolongation, the proposed return loop, or benefits for other liquids, vessels or continuous processes.
